findings.text: Exposes an optimistic spinning acquisition helper for mutexes that optionally participates in wound-wait deadlock handling and optionally acts on behalf of an already queued waiter, returning success when the lock was taken by spinning and failure otherwise, with an alternate build variant that never spins and always reports failure.

When no waiter object is supplied the spinning path first probes whether spinning on the current holder is allowed and then serializes against other spinners through a queued spin lock, releasing that serialization on success and on failure, while the waiter-backed path skips the probe and the serialization.

Provides small helpers to attempt immediate acquisition while reporting the current holder, to extract the holder from the combined owner word, and to resolve the holder for wound-wait handling for plain and realtime mutex kinds.
The holder is derived from an atomic word by clearing flag bits, with a null mutex reference yielding no holder, so the word simultaneously carries ownership and state flags.

The holder-spinning predicates require the caller to have disabled preemption, treat a pending reschedule as a reason to stop, and treat a holder that is no longer running on a processor as a reason to stop.

Spinning on a specific holder continues only while the recorded holder remains the current holder, polling holder liveness and reschedule state with a relaxed pause between checks and additionally consulting wound-wait gating when a deadlock context is present.

Wound-wait spinning is abandoned when the acquiring context already holds other locks and a published context is observed, when a non-queued spinner observes queued waiters, and when a queued spinner is no longer first in line.
Exposes a queued spin lock with lock and unlock operations plus an internal helper that waits for a successor or reclaims the tail, built on per processor nodes and an encoded tail word.

The queue object holds an encoded tail word while each per processor node holds a grant flag, links to predecessor and successor, and an encoded processor identity, with an unlocked tail value distinct from any encoded identity.

Processor identities are offset when stored so that a reserved value can represent the unlocked state, with helpers to encode, decode through per processor storage, and recover the identity from a node.

Acquisition initializes the local node and exchanges into the tail, succeeding immediately when previously unlocked and otherwise linking after a predecessor and waiting for grant or cancellation; cancellation stabilizes the predecessor link, then resolves the successor or reclaims the tail, then splices neighbours; release hands off directly when a successor is already linked and otherwise resolves the successor before granting.

Publication of node fields precedes linking to the predecessor with ordering sufficient for cross processor visibility, tail updates pair acquire and release semantics, and successor grant uses ordered stores and loads.
In the non-debug build the common lock handling, waiter release, and waiter wake helpers compile to empty statements with no state change.
For the realtime build variant shown here the wound-wait add, check, acquired-accounting, and kill-check helpers are inert shims that perform no action, with value-returning ones indicating no error.

Successful wound-wait acquisition increments the per context acquisition count and publishes the context into the mutex, while debug builds additionally validate pairing of acquire and release calls, outstanding contention, and class consistency.

All waiter enumeration, predecessor and successor lookup, and deadlock scan helpers require the wait lock to be held by the caller, with lockdep assertions enforcing the rule for plain and realtime mutex kinds.

Plain mutex waiters are kept in a circular list anchored by a first waiter pointer with wraparound termination, while realtime mutex waiters are kept in a balanced tree keyed by entry nodes with null termination at the ends.
The deadlock scan walks every waiter under the wait lock, ignores entries without a wound-wait context, and stops at the first entry where either the wait-die or the wound action triggers.

Wait-die mode wakes a younger waiter that conflicts with an older holder and records no wound, while wound mode marks an older holder as wounded and queues a wake for it when it is not the current task, each clearing blocked-on state to avoid unresolvable proxy cycles.

Context ordering prefers older stamps as winners using signed difference, with an additional realtime priority and deadline tie break where earlier deadlines and higher priorities win before falling back to stamp order.

Observed wound-wait state includes a per mutex published context and class, and per context acquisition count, stamp, wounded flag, mode selector, completion flag, contending lock reference, class reference, and task reference.

The fast acquisition path publishes the context before checking for waiters with a full barrier so that concurrent waiter insertion cannot be missed, and on observing waiters it takes the wait lock, rescans for die or wound actions, releases, and drains queued wakes with preemption controlled around the drain.
Wait lock acquisition and release wrap a raw spin lock with interrupt state save and restore, and several helpers assert the lock is already held rather than acquiring it.

For plain mutexes the presence of waiters is tested by inspecting flag bits in the owner word without requiring the wait lock, while for realtime mutexes it is tested by checking whether the waiter tree is non-empty with the wait lock held.

Holder task references are treated as stable across the spin because preemption is disabled, which acts as a read-side critical section, combined with an ordering barrier that separates the holder identity check from subsequent holder state reads.

Spinning and queue waiting treat a pending reschedule and observed holder or predecessor preemption as cancellation triggers, with the outer optimistic path forcing a running state and a schedule point before reporting failure when a reschedule is pending.
Waking a waiter to die or wound its holder clears blocked-on tracking with a waking marker before queueing the wake, preventing circular blocked-on relationships from persisting across the wakeup.

Wound handling tolerates a missing holder or missing published context by taking no action, and the realtime owner helper observed here yields no holder, so callers must handle absence without dereference.

The optimistic spinning helper and the queued spin lock operations serve as slowpath entry points invoked with preemption already disabled, reporting success or failure to the caller rather than blocking.

Exposes helpers to scan waiters for conflicts, to evaluate wait-die and wound actions, to check whether the current context must abort, to record a kill decision, and to publish context on the fast path.

Observed mutex state includes a combined atomic owner word, an embedded queued spin lock, a wait serialization lock, and a pointer to the first waiter, with waiter entries carrying list linkage and optional wound-wait context.
The debug waiter-wake helper requires the wait lock to be held and warns when no first waiter is recorded or when the waiter identity marker does not match the waiter itself.

Wound-wait abort evaluation first exempts contexts holding nothing, then in wound mode aborts only when marked wounded, and in wait-die mode aborts when the published holder is older or any earlier waiter carries a context, recording contention on abort when already holding locks.
Checks of first-waiter identity and waiter presence are performed with race annotations or atomic reads, acknowledging concurrent mutation without holding the wait lock in the spin path.
